The error shown on the screen is "error[E0499]: cannot borrow `x` as mutable more than once." This error occurs when trying to borrow a mutable variable (`x`) more than once, which is not allowed in Rust.

To rebuild the project, you would click on the "Rebuild" button.

VISUAL_TOKEN_BUDGET_FINDING.what_the_old_eval_missed: this file measured ONE fixture with unusually large text and judged quality by eyeballing a single answer string. That never surfaced the defect below.
VISUAL_TOKEN_BUDGET_FINDING.the_defect: a 1512x982 screen is ~1890 Qwen2-VL visual tokens, and feeding that many drives this checkpoint into REPETITION COLLAPSE on ordinary screenshots. Asked for the IPv4 address on a legible settings dialog it answered 'The The The The The ...'; asked what a button said on a code-editor screenshot it did the same; asked for an error code it regurgitated the source.
VISUAL_TOKEN_BUDGET_FINDING.the_fix: cap the image at DESCRIBE_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS = 380000 (~764x496, ~459 visual tokens) before generating. Aspect-ratio preserving; images already under the cap are untouched; any failure returns the original path so it costs the speedup and never the answer.

before_after_single_samples.orig_error_code_before: 7945 ms, describes the borrow error but gives no code

the_working_band.floor: ~216 visual tokens (0.35 scale) - accuracy 0/8, text unreadable

VISUAL_TOKEN_BUDGET_FINDING.WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_FIX: SUPERSEDED — see MODEL_COMPARISON_2026_07_31.CORRECTION_TO_AN_EARLIER_CLAIM. This key asserted '2/12 to 4/12 at EVERY resolution' and 'still not reliable', which contradicted the correction recorded later in this same file. That figure came from UNCAPPED resolutions — the regime where the model collapses into repetition — and a harder question set; it was never a measurement of the shipped configuration. Measured at the shipped cap it is 54/72 = 75.0%, evenly 18/24 across all three fixtures. What DOES stand: the cap removes a failure mode and ~5x of latency, and the model still occasionally invents an error code, so an answer is a reading and not a guarantee.

VISUAL_TOKEN_BUDGET_FINDING.WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_FIX_ORIGINAL_TEXT: screen-VQA is still not reliable. Across three fixtures and four checkable facts the model scored 2/12 to 4/12 at EVERY resolution, and even after the cap it hallucinated an error code that is not on screen. The cap removes a failure MODE and 5x of latency; it does not make this 2B checkpoint good at reading screens. A better VLM is the real answer and remains unevaluated.

MODEL_COMPARISON_2026_07_31.question: is there a better VLM than the pinned Qwen2-VL-2B for reading screens?
MODEL_COMPARISON_2026_07_31.method: 12 checkable facts (error codes, an IP address, a DNS server, button labels, a source filename, a security type) across three fixtures with 12px/13px/large text, 6 samples each = 72 evaluations per model, at the SHIPPED visual-token cap. Harness committed as compare_models.py.
MODEL_COMPARISON_2026_07_31.verdict: NO-GO on a swap. The incumbent wins on EVERY axis - accuracy, latency and memory - against both newer-generation candidates, including the most-downloaded mlx-community VLM.
MODEL_COMPARISON_2026_07_31.prompting_was_checked_first: a bare question versus one with an answer-shape suffix changed a single case from 2/3 to 3/3 and a third phrasing collapsed to '111111...', so phrasing genuinely matters. But re-running both candidates WITH the suffix left them at 25% and 33% - prompting does not explain the gap.
MODEL_COMPARISON_2026_07_31.CORRECTION_TO_AN_EARLIER_CLAIM: PR #157 and its commit stated screen-VQA scores '2/12 to 4/12 at every resolution' and is 'still not reliable'. That figure came from a run spanning UNCAPPED resolutions - the regime where the model collapses into repetition - and a harder question set. Measured properly at the shipped cap it is 75%, evenly 18/24 across all three fixtures. The cap fix was right; the characterisation of what remains was too harsh.
what_this_does_not_settle: three synthetic fixtures and twelve facts is a small set; it measures SCREEN TEXT reading, not general vision
mlx-vlm 0.6.4's Qwen3-VL support may itself be immature - this cannot distinguish 'the model is worse' from 'the port is worse' without a reference implementation

the OCR-specialised architectures mlx-vlm now supports (dots_ocr, deepseekocr, paddleocr_vl and four others) were NOT evaluated; transcribe-then-ask with the resident 4B LLM is a different design worth measuring separately
MODEL_COMPARISON_2026_07_31.housekeeping: both losing checkpoints (4,685 MB) were deleted immediately rather than left to accumulate, which is how 7.3 GB of rejected candidates built up before.
